question: When a machine takes over a craft's repetitive task, as computers did for typesetters, do the human jobs vanish or change, and what does that say about graphic designers and AI today?

issues.note: The film opens on the cork board with the -17% figure, then cuts straight to a blank title card with only a lamp. The statistic comes before any setup, so the cut feels abrupt.
The cut goes from a warm, bright type-case image to a dark Linotype hall with no visible link between hand-set and machine-set type. The lower-third text is also tiny and low-contrast.

The 'road to extinction' quote sits on the Linotype room, then the next shot is a small 1975 computer scene with a different style and a window of stars. Narration says 'cold' type, but nothing in the picture explains what is cold about it.
The 'certain to disappear' quote plays over a dark, empty wall, then the film cuts to the type case. The 'did not vanish' turn is not shown in the picture.
The change of place and mood is abrupt, from the type case to the Printing-Composing street. The caption '...limited by computers' fades out across the cut and looks cut off.
The frames show the poster wall and the screen shifting around. The narration, 'Can the BLS see a change', has no matching image.
The poster wall cuts to the Linotype room, which has nothing to do with 'the comparison'. The caption is faint and unreadable at the cut.
The cut crosses between very different scenes (type case, poster wall) while the caption is mid-line.
